hooks.name: adop-capture-user-turn
hooks.description: Captures each user prompt into the workload requirements ledger when the active run exists.

hooks.name: adop-inject-run-context-session
hooks.description: Injects in-flight run state at session start so a resumed or compacted orchestrator recovers from disk instead of re-asking the human. Read-only, never blocks. SessionStart is the IDE-side activation trigger; the CLI equivalent is AgentSpawn, wired separately below. Whichever trigger the running surface does not implement is inert, so both are declared.

hooks.name: adop-inject-run-context-spawn
hooks.description: CLI counterpart of adop-inject-run-context-session. AgentSpawn fires when an agent is activated and carries no tool context; stdout is added to context on exit 0. Identical payload-free read of workloads/*/run/context.json.

hooks.name: adop-block-credentials
hooks.description: Denies writes containing hardcoded credentials or infrastructure identifiers.

hooks.name: adop-enforce-template-codegen
hooks.description: Denies hand-written pipeline artifacts under workloads/*/{scripts,dags,sql}/; those are rendered from schema-validated specs only. config/ stays writable because specs live there.

hooks.name: adop-phase-1-gate
hooks.description: ENFORCING. Denies subagent spawning until context.json and the explicit human discovery answers are complete. 'subagent' is Kiro's built-in spawn tool; the regex also covers the camelCase and snake_case spellings other surfaces use.

hooks.name: adop-auditor-write-scope
hooks.description: DEFENCE IN DEPTH. Restricts the requirements-auditor to its report and append-only audit trace outputs. Primary enforcement is the permissions.rules block in .kiro/agents/requirements-auditor.json, because Kiro does not put the calling agent's identity in the PreToolUse payload; this hook only adds a second layer when ADOP_AGENT_NAME is exported by the spawning process.

hooks.name: adop-validate-artifacts
hooks.description: ENFORCING. Syntax errors and credentials in a pending artifact are denied before the write. Every check runs on the payload content, so it does not need the file on disk.

hooks.name: adop-validate-artifacts-post
hooks.description: ADVISORY. Second pass on the file as written, for content that reached disk through the write tool. Kiro does not treat a non-zero exit on PostToolUse as a block, so findings are reported only.

hooks.name: adop-validate-artifacts-on-save
hooks.description: ADVISORY. Covers content that reached disk by a route with no tool_input -- a shell heredoc, say -- which no PreToolUse write matcher can see. PostFileSave matches on the FILE PATH, and validate_artifacts falls back to reading the file, so this pass works without a tool payload. Advisory only: PostFileSave cannot block.

hooks.name: adop-deploy-gate
hooks.description: Optional Phase 5 deploy gate. Disabled by default; set ADOP_DEPLOY_GATE=1 to deny deploy mutations (Glue job/table create-update, IAM role policy, Lake Formation grants/tags, job starts, DAG upload) until run/requirements_audit.json passes and preflight has written run/deploy_gate.json. Runs on every PreToolUse and classifies the call itself. Non-deploy calls return immediately without importing anything.

hooks.name: adop-cedar-gate
hooks.description: Evaluates every tool call against the Cedar policies in shared/policies/ as the main-conversation principal (onboarding). Sub-agents carry their own adop-cedar-gate hook with --principal, because Kiro sends no agent identity in the payload. No matcher: the engine classifies the call. Fails closed.
